articles.headline: USMNT star Christian Pulisic signs new AC Milan contract through 2031
articles.description: United States star Christian Pulisic has signed a new contract with AC Milan through 2031.
articles.body:
United States star Christian Pulisic has signed a new contract with AC Milan through 2031.

The deal for Pulisic, 28, was reported by ESPN on Wednesday and confirmed on Friday, a day after AC Milan announced plans for their new stadium.

"Captain America's Rossonero mission continues," wrote AC Milan on Friday.

Pulisic's deal was due to expire in June 2027, but he has committed his future to the Rossoneri on a contract that will take him beyond the next World Cup.

"There's a lot of emotions, I'm really proud to re-sign here in Milan because I'm really just in love with this team, this club, everything about it," Pulisic said in an interview on the club's social media pages. "The feeling that I got, the support from the fans through all of the good and bad times, I knew immediately that this was the place for me.:

He joined AC Milan in 2023 from Chelsea for a fee in the region of €22 million ($24.4m). At the Serie A club, Pulisic has 44 goals and 28 assists across his 141 appearances and was the club's top scorer in the 2024-25 season.

"Milan has given me everything, it feels like home for me," he said. "It's where I want to spend my next years because I'm just really happy here, I love it here, my family loves it here. I want to continue to give everything and bring this club to the top.

He added: "I look at my whole life as a book, to be honest, and i feel like this is the most important chapter right now."

Pulisic signed for Borussia Dortmund back in 2015 and established himself as one of the best young players in the Bundesliga. Chelsea signed him for £58m ($71.7m) in 2018, and he won the 2021 Champions League there.

But injury disrupted his progress at Chelsea, and in 2023, AC Milan saw off competition from Juventus, Lyon and Galatasaray to sign him.

- Pulisic staying in Milan reflects his club career: Good, but not quite great

- Cavan Sullivan turned 17 last month, but he's already playing like an MLS MVP

- Ex-USMNT star Eddie Johnson to train 3-year-old removed from Florida soccer game

Pulisic missed most of AC Milan's preseason due to the injury he sustained during the World Cup. But after a steady reintegration into the first team under Ruben Amorim, he has become an integral part of the manager's Milan blueprint, playing in the No. 10 role and on the wing.

Pulisic's new deal follows the unveiling of AC Milan's new stadium, which will be ready in 2031. The clubs said in a news release Thursday that the deal represented "one of the largest stadium naming rights agreements in global sport."

At the international level, Pulisic has established himself as a key player for the USMNT with 33 goals in 90 appearances. He played in the 2022 and 2026 World Cups for the USMNT and won U.S. Soccer Male Player of the Year in 2017, 2019, 2021 and 2023.

articles.headline: Kompany to sit out Bayern-Dortmund after leaving hospital
articles.description: Vincent Kompany won't be on the sidelines for Bayern's match against Borussia Dortmund following his hospitalization last week.
articles.body:
MUNICH -- Bayern Munich are not allowing coach Vincent Kompany to be part of their plans for Saturday's Klassiker against Bundesliga rival Borussia Dortmund following his collapse and hospitalization last week.

Assistant coach Aaron Danks said on Friday there were orders not to discuss the game with Kompany, even though he's out of hospital and recovering at home.

"We don't talk to him about football. We've been given clear instructions there," Danks said. "He needs to recover and spend time with his family. We're not getting him involved so he can be fully back at it when he returns."

Danks oversaw a 6-1 win over Magdeburg in the German Cup on Wednesday. Saturday's game against Dortmund is likely to see Harry Kane return to action after winning the Ballon d'Or on Monday.

Danks said not much has changed in how Bayern are training for the game, adding that Kompany's assistants aren't "mini-Vinnies" but have skill sets which complement each other to work together in his absence.

Bayern board member for sport Max Eberl told German broadcaster ARD on Wednesday that Kompany was treated for meningeal irritation, which is an inflammation of the tissue around the brain or spinal cord.

Before his collapse, Kompany had also been struggling with a viral infection and a hip injury.

articles.headline: Inside how Titans were convinced to trade their best player
articles.description: Titans GM Mike Borgonzi got an offer he couldn't refuse, and now Jeffery Simmons is a Chicago Bear.
articles.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- Titans general manager Mike Borgonzi said he fielded numerous calls from other teams to trade for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons as he took over as Tennessee's general manager in 2024. Borgonzi didn't take any offers seriously because he had no intentions of trading the team's All-Pro player.

Trading Simmons wasn't on Borgonzi's bingo card when he awoke Wednesday. Then he received a call from Chicago Bears general manager Ryan Poles, whom he had worked with in the Kansas City Chiefs' personnel department from 2009-21. It was one the GM couldn't refuse. 

Now Borgonzi and the Titans have to figure out how they'll go about replacing a franchise cornerstone as they rebuild.

News of Thursday's blockbuster trade surprised Simmons, who had just told the media on Wednesday that neither his agent nor the team had informed him of any intentions to move him to another team. Simmons, 29, said he wanted to stay in Nashville and get the Titans back on track. Titans right tackle JC Latham said Thursday the look of disgust on Simmons' face when the news broke made it clear he was disappointed. Borgonzi had signed Simmons to a three-year, $105 million deal in June and called him a "pillar of the franchise that embodies what it means to be a Titan."

Then Poles called with an offer for Simmons that included a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 first-round pick, and a 2027 fourth-round pick. Getting two first-round picks for a defensive tackle had never happened to Borgonzi -- or throughout the NFL in the common draft era (since 1967), per ESPN Research.

"At no point anytime since I've been here did we ever try to trade Jeffery Simmons," Borgonzi said Thursday. "We've gotten a lot of phone calls on Jeff really since I've been hired here, but it's never really crossed my mind. And I got a phone call late last night from a person that I've known for a while, Ryan Poles, he's GM with the Bears. We considered the compensation, and it was too good to pass up."

Following the call, Borgonzi's first move was to discuss the deal with Titans coach Robert Saleh. Like the GM, Saleh had Simmons earmarked as a guy the organization was going to build around for years to come. Saleh had recently pointed to Simmons as the best defensive tackle in football and credited the veteran for inspiring the Titans' second-half resurgence on the road in Week 6 against the Indianapolis Colts that led to their only win of the season.  

Borgonzi and Saleh didn't sleep much Wednesday night mulling over the deal. 

The next step was getting the signoff from Titans controlling owner Amy Adams-Strunk, who has a close relationship with Simmons dating back to when the organization drafted the former Mississippi State player with the No. 19 pick in 2019.

articles.headline: Mikel Arteta warning to Max Dowman after red card: 'We are not in Disneyland'
articles.description: Mikel Arteta has said Arsenal are "very disappointed" after their appeal over Max Dowman's red card at Fleetwood Town was dismissed but warned the teenager must adapt to top level football because "otherwise we are in Disneyland."
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has said Arsenal are "very disappointed" after their appeal over Max Dowman's red card at Fleetwood Town was dismissed but warned the teenager must adapt to top-level football because "otherwise we are in Disneyland."

The 16-year-old was sent off in Tuesday's Carabao Cup penalty shootout defeat after reacting to a strong challenge from Harrison Neal. Dowman will now serve a three-game suspension after the appeal was rejected by an independent panel.

Arteta was criticised in some quarters for his angry reaction to Dowman as he left the field. Speaking on Friday ahead of the weekend Premier League trip to Liverpool, Arteta suggested the pair had spoken about the possible provocation from the League Two side before the game.

"I haven't seen the reaction to my reaction [to Dowman], whether it is positive or negative," Arteta said.

He also went on to reference Dowman's second red card this month, having been sent off while playing for England's under-19s.

"But you need to understand the context, the relationship that I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out.

"I don't know. You can have a lot of reactions. If you see the reaction of my father and my mother with me, someday you will say, I don't like the reaction. For me, it was the best reaction ever to be able to be who I am. But you want to always see the best reaction and the beautiful one.

"You want to see the reaction of his teammates? When they have to play with ten, you want to see that?

"What do you expect? I don't know. And the England ones, they are his age, 16, the same. What is their reaction? That's the reaction. That's the level and that's the reaction. And whether it is right or wrong, that's the reaction.

"But the reaction when I don't win, you know what the reaction is? I'm p----- off, big time. So we need to be ready for that. This is the environment and this is the reality.

"Otherwise, we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland. We are in the Premier League at this level and we look after him so much that you cannot imagine. But at the same time, we're going to demand him like anybody else because he needs to earn the right to play. Otherwise, the rest of the boys, what are they going to tell me? You need to be fair. Let's go."

Regarding the appeal, Arteta said: "Very disappointed, to be fair. Especially with the reckless tackles that he received, and then his reaction is minimal in relation to the action. Disappointed that it's not been overturned after looking at the action back, to be fair.

"It is what it is. We have put every argument on the table to make a case for it. Not only the action, obviously, that it's evident, and when you look it back in slow motion, the previous action and Max's action, it's clear that obviously we have a very different opinion.

"And on top of that, I think you have to read the context of the player, the age, and what happened previously."

articles.headline: Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso: 'No discussion' over Estêvão loan move
articles.description: Xabi Alonso has said there have been "no discussions" about sending Estêvão on loan despite the Brazil star's limited minutes this term.
articles.body:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has said there have been "no discussions" about sending Estêvão out on loan despite the Brazil star's limited minutes this term.

The 19-year-old was a revelation last season after joining from Palmeiras but has played only 172 minutes under Alonso and is yet to start in the Premier League.

He remained an unused substitute as Chelsea exited the Carabao Cup to Liverpool at Anfield on Wednesday, after which the manager suggested that the winger was still acclimatising to the physicality of English football.

So far he has found his way into the side blocked by a favoured front three of Morgan Rogers, Cole Palmer and João Pedro, though even when players have been unavailable Alonso has still preferred other options over the Brazilian.

"Sure, he will play," Alonso said. "The season is long and there will be moments for everyone.

"It's a process, for the team, for [Estêvão], for myself. But I'm sure that in the season, he will have his games, his minutes. We are still early in the season but he will be there."

Asked whether the winger could be allowed to leave in January, Alonso said: "No discussions about [a loan]."

Estêvão was one of few bright spots in a miserable year for Chelsea last season. There had been significant anticipation about his arrival, agreed in the summer of 2024 but delayed for a year allowing him to remain with his boyhood club in Brazil, and he quickly became a favourite amongst supporters.

His stoppage-time winner against champions Liverpool at Stamford Bridge in October was arguably Chelsea's best moment of the season, rivalled only perhaps by the 3-0 win over Barcelona a month later when Estêvão scored a spectacular individual goal.

His season was ended prematurely in April due to a hamstring injury, causing him to miss the World Cup.

- Alonso: Estêvão will 'have his moment' at Chelsea

Alonso said Estêvão is fully recovered and that his attitude has been good, and that it is now a matter of waiting for his moment in the team.

"It's not about attitude, it's been about the context of games," he said. "He's a great guy. It's an adaptation, after the first year and the injury. We are still in October. He will be important."

Chelsea face Manchester United at Stamford Bridge on Saturday looking to hit back from losing at home to Tottenham a week ago, though they will do so without Maxence Lacroix, who is set to be out until after the November international break with a hamstring injury.

Moisés Caicedo, however, is fit despite picking up a knock at Anfield.

"I saw a better version of ourselves on Wednesday [against Liverpool] than I saw on Saturday," Alonso said. "The result at the end wasn't good, but I want to see more of the good version of us.

articles.headline: Jets dealing with defensive injuries for matchup vs. Raiders, RB Ashton Jeanty
articles.description: Jets nose tackle T'Vondre Sweat has been ruled out with a knee injury, and rookie edge rusher David Bailey, unable to practice this week due to a strained groin, is listed as doubtful.
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- The New York Jets' defense, called out this week by Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty, will be down at least one and probably two starters for Sunday's game at MetLife Stadium.

Nose tackle T'Vondre Sweat was ruled out Friday with a knee injury, and rookie edge rusher David Bailey, unable to practice this week due to a strained groin, is listed as doubtful. Both were injured last Sunday in the Jets' 28-25 loss to the Miami Dolphins.

This increases the pressure on the front seven, which has struggled to stop the run. Since Week 3, the Jets are allowing 153 yards per game, which ranks 31st in the NFL.

They have bulletin-board material as motivation, thanks to Jeanty, who told Las Vegas reporters on Wednesday, "They have a couple of guys out there that don't really want to tackle." He didn't name names.

The quote made the rounds at One Jets Drive.

"This is the NFL, and I get it. Everybody's motivated by certain things," Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Friday. "But man, your true motivation is each week you get a chance to play, and I think that's about it. But words are always said between players, and that's just what it is. Our guys will be ready to play."

Jets defensive players, likely instructed to keep quiet, downplayed the quote.

"Obviously, certain things add a little more fuel to the fire, but at the end of the day, I have to go out there and do my job," safety Minkah Fitzpatrick said. "I feel like most of the guys in this locker room operate in the same fashion."

Privately, some players said they were surprised by Jeanty's comment, considering his own struggles. Jeanty, the No. 6 overall pick in 2025, rushed for only 15 yards in last week's 35-21 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. He is averaging 3.1 yards per rush for the season as the Raiders (3-4), ranked 31st in rushing offense, are on a four-game losing streak.

The Jets (2-5) have dropped two straight.

The 366-pound Sweat, acquired in an offseason trade with the Tennessee Titans, is one of their best run stuffers. He likely will be replaced by rookie Darrell Jackson Jr.

"Losing [Sweat], I mean, that's always a huge deal for us," Glenn said. "But the thing is we've got guys behind him that are going to come in and do a good job for us."

Bailey, who leads the Jets with 5.5 sacks, would be replaced by Will McDonald IV. Drafted No. 2 overall, Bailey is one of the leading candidates for Defensive Rookie of the Year.

Once again, the status of running back Breece Hall (quadriceps) remains up on the air. He practiced all week on a limited basis and is listed as questionable. He has missed four straight games. Backup Braelon Allen has produced two 100-yard rushing games in Hall's absence.

Glenn said they want Hall to hit certain markers in his rehab before they play him in a game.

articles.headline: Barcelona's Flick on Yamal's Ballon d'Or setback: He reacted well
articles.description: Barcelona coach Hansi Flick said Lamine Yamal has reacted like a champion to missing out on the Ballon d'Or to Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane.
articles.body:
Barcelona coach Hansi Flick said Lamine Yamal has reacted like a champion to missing out on the Ballon d'Or to Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane.

Yamal, 19, was among the favourites to win the coveted individual prize, which was handed out at a gala held at the London Palladium last Monday.

However, after finishing second behind Paris Saint-Germain's Ousmane Dembélé last year, he came third this time, behind Kane and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé.

 

"Harry Kane also deserved to win this prize," Flick said in a news conference ahead of Saturday's LaLiga match against Alavés at Spotify Camp Nou.

"You know my opinion about Lamine. He is on this level to win this trophy. I am very proud about Lamine. He reacted good in my opinion and has been focused in training. This is how champions respond.

"I am just happy [the Ballon d'Or] is now over. Now we can focus on other things."

Yamal did not leave the gala empty-handed, taking home the Kopa Trophy, awarded to the male best player under the age of 21, for the third consecutive year.

After accepting the award, he said Barça teammate Pau Cubarsí deserved the prize more than him.

"I have said this to the team, the words Lamine said after he got the trophy, about Cubarsí, were great," Flick said.

"For me, it was clear. Pau normally deserves to win this trophy. Lamine also won it in the last two years. It's the best time to give Pau this trophy after an incredible season and excellent World Cup."

After back-to-back defeats to PSG and Madrid, Barça are looking to get back to winning ways this weekend when they host Alavés in the league.

Despite the losses, Flick is optimistic of the LaLiga leader's chances of success this season, although he is increasingly worried about the injuries piling up in defence.

"There is a long, long way until the end of the season where you can win titles," the German coach said.

"Nothing really bad happens [in October]. Of course we lost against Real. No one here loves that, not me, the players or the fans. We have to accept it and learn.

"If you see Jules [Koundé], Xavi Espart, Eric García and Andreas Christensen [are all injured]. Four defenders. Plus [midfielder Dani] Olmo. It's not easy to manage. We have to find solutions."

With just Cubarsi, Gerard Martín, João Cancelo and Alejandro Balde available at the back this weekend, Flick confirmed solutions could include playing young midfielder Brian Fariñas at full-back or Frenkie de Jong at centre-back.

Long-term, the club could turn to the transfer market in January.

"We are always looking for what is best for team and what can improve the team," Flick said when asked if he wants to sign a centre-back.

"This is what we are doing. We will see. We have more weeks until January. We discuss a lot every day. If we can do something, maybe we will do it."

articles.headline: Ruben Amorim 'not in danger' - AC Milan chief makes 'Top Gun' vow
articles.description: AC Milan coach Ruben Amorim has been backed by the club's owner via a famous "Top Gun" reference.
articles.body:
AC Milan coach Ruben Amorim has been backed by the club's owner via a famous "Top Gun" reference.

Amorim joined Milan this summer after he was sacked as Manchester United boss. Despite sitting seven points from the top of Serie A, he has received backing from American owner Gerry Cardinale.

Asked by Gazzetta dello Sport if he still supported Amorim, Cardinale said: "Yes, and I have full faith in him. At the end of 'Top Gun' -- 'my' movie -- Tom Cruise says a great line: 'I'm not leaving my wingman.' And I'm not leaving Ruben.

"He is in no danger whatsoever. I will stand by his side. I won't make the mistakes made in recent years. He is my manager, and we'll keep working together until we manage to make the step up. You can't win if you keep switching managers. I chose Amorim.

"If I had made a mistake, I'd admit it, but I don't think I did. He learned a lot from what happened at Manchester United, and I hired him because he explained the mistakes made there to me.

"He has the right culture; he's a leader, a manager and a well-prepared coach. At Milanello, the atmosphere is different from the last four years. That is down to him.

"He's learning, and the team needs to find cohesion, understand how to rotate players, and keep scoring plenty of goals and winning. For me, a draw is a defeat. A point isn't the aim of the game: three points are. Only with wins can we bridge the gap with the leaders."

Milan lost their first Serie A game of the season on Wednesday night, 4-2 against Bologna. They were also beaten 3-0 by Bournemouth in the Europa League as Amorim returned to England.

They sit fifth in the league ahead of this weekend's derby against leaders Inter, a key chance to cut the deficit.

Cardinale insists his side can still win the Scudetto.

"It's absolutely possible, 100%," he said. "And I say this without meaning to sound arrogant. I wake up every morning hoping for a small glimmer of hope, that Inter will start drawing instead of winning and that we'll start putting together a series of victories.

"Winning is the only thing that matters to me, but let's take it one game at a time, gaining ground on those ahead of us, day after day."

After missing the first four games of the season with an ankle injury, No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa will make his regular-season debut Wednesday, ESPN's Shams Charania reported.

Dybantsa's arrival could give the Wizards one of the best starting lineups in the Eastern Conference -- which would be quite a change of pace for a team that hasn't won 20 games in a season since 2022-23. Anthony Davis has been explosive and productive through four games. Trae Young is averaging 22 points and a league-best 11 assists per game. And Kyshawn George is up to 18 PPG as he continues to make strides as an all-around NBA contributor. Add Dybantsa to that mix and there's legitimate reason for excitement in Washington.

The only downside is that Dybantsa should command plenty of playing time, which could further squeeze an overcrowded Wizards rotation. articles.headline: Tottenham's Pedro Porro keen on future LaLiga return
articles.description: Pedro Porro has denied receiving offers from Barcelona and Real Madrid this summer but the Tottenham right-back has said that he would like to return to play in Spain one day.
articles.body:
Pedro Porro has denied receiving offers from Barcelona and Real Madrid this summer but the Tottenham right-back has said that he would like to return to play in Spain one day.

Porro, who signed a contract extension with Tottenham until June 2031 before helping Spain win the World Cup in the summer, told El Larguero: "Obviously, I'm really looking forward to returning to Spain one day. It's my country and I like the league.

"Right now, it would be very unfair to talk about anything other than my club because I'm under contract. They [Spurs] have shown me a lot of respect, which is mutual."

Asked if Madrid and Barcelona made an offer to sign him in the last transfer window, Porro said: "No. There was interest because they ask what your situation is but there wasn't real interest. There were rumours, but I was focused on doing well for my country.

"If there's genuine interest, they call you directly, and that didn't happen. Some clubs did enquire to find out my situation, but there was no genuine interest. I didn't want to pay too much attention to it."

Porro, 27, believes Madrid and Barça may have been deterred by Tottenham's high asking price. "Probably," he said. "They [Spurs] rate me as one of the best.

"But I sorted out my contract renewal before the World Cup so I could have peace of mind during the tournament, because that has a big impact on your performance."

Porro made 47 appearances in all competitions last season, the most of anyone in Roberto De Zerbi's squad. He insists he is happy at the north London club. "I feel very much loved and that's very important to me," he said.

"They [Spurs] offered me a good contract, although if I'd waited until after the World Cup I'd have got a bit more out of it."

Porro joined Spurs on a permanent transfer from Sporting CP in the summer of 2023 having initially signed on loan in January 2023.

- Harry Kane thanks Tottenham, pays tribute to England after Ballon d'Or win

- Tottenham's rare win at Chelsea signals progress under De Zerbi

In the event he decides to return to Spain in the future, Porro believes he would have no problem adapting to any LaLiga club.

Asked if he would be better suited to play at Barcelona or Real Madrid, the former Real Valladolid player said: "I see myself as a player who can adapt to anything. I've adapted to the Premier League, which is by no means easy."

articles.body:
Portland Trail Blazers (3-1, fifth in the Western Conference) vs. Utah Jazz (1-4, 13th in the Western Conference)


              Salt Lake City; Saturday, 3 p.m. EDT


              BOTTOM LINE: Utah heads into the matchup with Portland as losers of three straight games.


              Utah finished 22-60 overall, 12-40 in Western Conference play and 14-27 at home during the 2025-26 season. The Jazz shot 46.7% from the field and 34.5% from 3-point range last season.


              Portland finished 42-40 overall and 29-23 in Western Conference play during the 2025-26 season. The Trail Blazers averaged 8.3 steals, 5.5 blocks and 16.5 turnovers per game last season.


              INJURIES: Jazz: Jusuf Nurkic: out (foot), Jaren Jackson Jr.: out (knee), Lauri Markkanen: day to day (wrist).


              Trail Blazers: Robert Williams III: out (knee), Shaedon Sharpe: out (meniscus), Ja Morant: day to day (hamstring).

articles.headline: Grizzlies play the Kings on 5-game win streak

articles.headlineJa: グリズリーズ、5連勝中のキングスと対戦

articles.body:
Sacramento Kings (0-5, 15th in the Western Conference) vs. Memphis Grizzlies (5-0, second in the Western Conference)


              Memphis, Tennessee; Saturday, 8 p.m. EDT


              BOTTOM LINE: Memphis will try to extend its five-game win streak with a victory against Sacramento.


              Memphis went 25-57 overall, 19-33 in Western Conference action and 14-27 at home during the 2025-26 season. The Grizzlies averaged 27.8 assists per game on 41.3 made field goals last season.


              Sacramento finished 22-60 overall and 14-38 in Western Conference play during the 2025-26 season. The Kings gave up 121.0 points per game while committing 19.7 fouls last season.


              The teams square off for the second time this season. The Grizzlies won the last meeting 123-112 on Oct. 26. Ty Jerome scored 31 points to help lead the Grizzlies to the win.


              INJURIES: Grizzlies: None listed.


              Kings: Ben Simmons: out for season (achilles), Keegan Murray: out (ankle), Dylan Cardwell: out (calf), Maxime Raynaud: out (knee).
